edits.value_json: 日 is a picture of the sun. Shang-period sources also report uses for daylight and as a unit of days, but do not establish which use came first.
A present-day Chinese dictionary lists 日 as an abbreviation for Japan. The supplied evidence does not establish when this use arose or whether it remains current.

Oracle-bone and bronze examples document 日 in early inscriptional traditions. The sources report oracle-bone uses for the sun, daylight, and a day unit, but do not verify the dates of the individual inscriptions. The documented script categories include oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, and seal forms; the evidence does not date every form or establish a detailed sequence of graphic changes.
